newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clarke says economy not in boom-bust cycle.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke says economy not in boom-bust cycle.

text.p: British Chancellor of the Exchequer (finance minister) Kenneth Clarke said in a television interview on Monday that strong growth in the UK economy would not lead to a recession.
Speaking on BBC Television's Newsnight, he said good economic figures would continue, and the country had prospects of sustained growth.

"Investment's been running well and getting stronger over the last year...Our exports are standing up despite the strong pound," Clarke said. "We have no balance of payments problem this time which we did in 1987."
He denied that the ruling Conservative government, trailing in the polls, had engineered a "boom" in the economy which would leave a difficult legacy for an incoming government.
He said the one "cloud on the horizon" was the possibility that the opposition Labour Party, if it were elected in May, would upset the economy with a July budget.
In the same interview, Labour economics spokesman Gordon Brown said current investment levels would not support a lasting recovery, although he said the economy was not actually booming.
"I think we're in danger of overheating because the fundamentals are not right," said Brown.
Asked about whether he would raise interest rates if he took over in May, and was requested to do so by governor of the Bank of England Eddie George, Brown refused to speculate.
